title: Make going through a door one continuous move of a live world, not a cut and a zoom
tier_reason: The CEO raised it directly, it is the difference between the interiors reading as a place and reading as a camera trick, and he has set an explicit verification bar on it.
ask:
Interiors (P-18, docs/design/15-interiors.md) ship: a coop and the farmhouse have rooms you walk into, the camera zooms through the door, and the farm is drawn through the walls. Two defects remain and they are the same defect seen twice.

WHAT THE CEO REPORTED, 2026-09-16
"When the zoom happens, the camera position can jump a bit. This makes things in the outer world (e.g. fences) suddenly hop to a new position and then zoom. This makes it feel like we've switched scenes and are doing a fake zoom." And then: "Can we fix this? Actually draw everything correctly? Can the world actually continue to simulate and update on the periphery of the room the player is in? Can we keep the world alive through this process, so it's not just a camera trick?"

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS
The world IS already alive. SimWorld never pauses when she goes through a door: brains tick, the hen wanders, crows arrive, crops advance at the day turn, weather rolls. This is not a simulation gap. It is a DRAWING gap -- world/farm.gd's _draw_room_backdrop is a simplified hand-written second pass (ground, boundary state, object sprite) and it does not draw crops, effects, or actors. Do not "make the world live"; it is live. Draw the world that is already running.

DEFECT 1 -- the position jump
use_door teleports her from page 0 to the room (page 2 for a coop, page 1 for the home), tens of tiles in world coordinates. The camera is a child of the player node and snaps with her (main.gd _refresh_camera_limits calls camera.reset_smoothing()). Then _zoom_through_door tweens zoom only. So the swap frame moves every world landmark to a new screen pixel, and the zoom starts after it.

The maths for fixing it is exact and already in the codebase. The backdrop maps farm space into room space as room_px = offset + farm_px * pitch, where offset is Farm.room_backdrop_offset(room, building_rect). So at the instant of the swap, putting the camera at offset + camera_farm_pos * pitch with zoom / pitch shows a pixel-identical view; from there one tween of BOTH position and zoom to her new centre is continuous by construction. Watch three Godot mechanics: the camera is parented to the player so camera.position is an offset from her; position_smoothing_enabled is on at speed 8 and will fight an explicit tween; and camera.limit_* clamps continuously, so the final limits must not be applied until the tween ends.

DEFECT 2 -- the content gap, which is why fixing the camera alone is not enough
Even with a perfect camera, crops and actors would pop out of existence on the swap frame, because they are not in the backdrop. That would move the seam rather than remove it.

THE PROPOSED MECHANISM -- verify before building on it
A SubViewport sharing the main viewport's World2D, with its own Camera2D positioned over the farm. That renders the same canvas world -- crops, actors, effects, weather -- using the code that already draws them, with no parallel implementation to drift. The backdrop then becomes that live texture drawn at scale pitch with the existing offset. It is the technique used for minimaps and portals.

TWO UNKNOWNS. SPIKE BOTH BEFORE WIRING ANYTHING IN.
  1. Does Godot 4.7 behave as expected with SubViewport.world_2d shared and a Camera2D inside the SubViewport driving it? Confirm the farm renders, and that CanvasLayer content (the HUD) does NOT leak into it.
  2. What does it cost? This draws the world twice per frame and the target is an Android tablet. Measure with tools/benchmark_sim.gd and on the device (tools/deploy_android.sh). A frame-rate regression on the tablet is not an acceptable price and the CEO has not agreed to one.
If either unknown comes back negative, STOP and report. Do not improvise a fallback -- the alternative (extending the hand-written pass to re-implement autotiled soil, growth stages, the watered chip, the ripe glow and every actor draw) is a second renderer that must be kept honest forever, and that is a design decision, not an implementation one.

THE VERIFICATION BAR, SET BY THE CEO
He asked: "If it's fixed, can you verify that it works as described before showing it to me again?" The answer given was yes, by measurement rather than by eye. Build the harness FIRST and baseline the CURRENT build with it, so there is a failing measurement before there is a fix:
  a. Per frame through a transition, log camera global position and zoom, and compute where a fixed world landmark (pick a fence corner at a known farm tile) lands on screen. Assert that screen path has no frame-to-frame discontinuity.
  b. Capture every frame and diff consecutive pairs. A smooth zoom gives a small steadily-changing difference; a jump or a content pop gives a spike. This is the stronger test because it catches causes nobody enumerated.
Do not show him anything until the spike in (b) is gone. tools/capture_coop_inside.tscn and tools/capture_interior_plate.tscn are the existing capture harnesses to build from.

ALSO PARKED, SMALLER, HIS WORDS: "let's plan to come back to the stutter in a second"
ui/menus.gd ENTER_DELAY_SECONDS is 0.10 -- the beat between the structure panel closing and the door transition starting. He confirmed the stutter is real but the current value may be too short against a 0.60s zoom. 0.20 is the obvious next try. It is marked [Playtest]. Do this one only after the above, and only with his word on the value.

HOUSE RULES THAT BIT THIS FEATURE ALREADY
  - A passing unit test on a gateway verb says nothing about whether the player can reach it. A room's doorway was a tile state and SPECIAL_OBJECTS is keyed on objects, so the verb worked and the tap did not; the CEO found it in play. Anything reached by tapping gets a test that starts at InputManager, in tools/test_runner.tscn. Scenario AX is the pattern.
  - Both suites green on every commit, plus the robot session and tools/check_gateway.py.
  - Another Claude session shares this working tree. Commit only your own files.
  - Run Godot with XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a scratch dir, or two sessions fight over user:// and the integration suite hangs.

FILES
  world/farm.gd            _draw_room_backdrop, room_backdrop_offset, _backdrop_active/_backdrop_rect
  main.gd                  _zoom_through_door, _refresh_camera_limits, _limit_to_room, DOOR_ZOOM_SECONDS
  systems/sim/sim_world.gd rooms registry, room_building_rect, world_pos_of_cell, room_exit_for
  docs/design/15-interiors.md   the whole design, and section 9 for what is and is not built
first_action: Build the frame-by-frame measurement harness and run it against the CURRENT build, so the position jump and the content pop are both measured before anything is changed.
source_message: Handed off 2026-09-16 from the session that built the interiors, at the CEO's suggestion, because the remaining work is well defined and does not need that session's history.
